source_credit: Charlie Munger: Poor Charlie's Almanack and his talks. Plain one-line maxims in our own words.

entries.text: Before you start a plan, ask what would make it fail. Then avoid those things.
You win more by avoiding dumb mistakes than by trying to be a genius.
Look at each problem from several angles. One way of thinking misses a lot.
Once you own something good, be patient. Most gains come from waiting.
Pick one simple idea that works and use it every single day.
Try to learn one new thing each day. Small daily gains add up over years.
Learn the common ways people misjudge things, you included. Ignoring them leads to surprises.
To change what people do, change what they get paid or praised for.
Avoid the games you do not understand. Play the ones where you know more.
Do not envy a rival. It costs you and gives you nothing back.
If a deal is too hard to understand, say no and move on.
Know the limits of what you know. Ask for help past that line.
Only sell what you would buy. Work with people you respect and enjoy.
Teach others what you know. Helping people learn more is worth your time.
When you notice you are copying others, stop. Ask if you would do it alone.
Do not lock in a choice out loud too early. You will defend it too long.
People return favors and slights. Be kind first, and watch for small gifts in deals.
Be extra careful judging people you like. Liking someone hides their faults.
When something feels urgent only because it is scarce, slow down and check its real value.
People link a feeling to the place they felt it. Give bad news somewhere else.
Do not follow advice just because of who gave it. Check whether it is right.
When many pressures push you toward yes at once, slow down before you agree.
A bad deal stays bad at any price. Walk away from it.
Use a checklist for hard jobs. Do not trust memory for the simple steps.
A great thing at a fair price beats an average thing at a cheap price.
Spend less than you earn and keep learning. Stay away from toxic people.
If you defend an idea because it feels like part of you, recheck it.
Going against the crowd only pays if you are right. Do the homework first.
Expect some losses. Keep them small and let your wins grow bigger.
Before you act, ask what happens next, and then what happens after that.
Write down each mistake and what caused it so you do not repeat it.
Read a little every day. Over years, what you know grows a lot.
Learn from many fields, like psychology, money and history. Problems rarely fit just one.
Deciding where each dollar goes is your most important job. Treat it that way.
Learn basic bookkeeping. It shows you how your business is really doing.
You will make many mistakes. Learn from them and keep going.
Steady wealth comes from good choices made slowly. Save part of what you earn, every time.
Keep your costs under your income and invest the difference. Learn what your work needs.
List the sure ways to fail at a goal. Then make a rule against each one.
Always do what you promised. Being unreliable ruins everything else you do well.
When something hurts you, turn it into work or let it go. Grudges get nothing done.
